title.title: Yau's nodal upper bound: true on surfaces, false above
title.subtitle: Claim: nodal length is at most $C\sqrt\lambda$ on every smooth surface; smooth metrics beat it in dimensions 3 and up

plain: How long are the still lines on a vibrating drum? On surfaces, as predicted; in higher dimensions, far longer

beats.text: Yau: the zero set of $-\Delta u = \lambda u$ has measure about $\sqrt\lambda$ (curves schematic)
On every smooth surface the release closes the gap down to $C\sqrt\lambda$
On $S^3$ and $S^2 \times T^2$ it fails; on $S^4 \times S^1$ by a fixed power

steps: On surfaces the bound holds, at the predicted rate
Above that, build wild metrics that trap vibrations in small regions
Glue those into exact modes whose zero sets are far too large

achievement.label: Yau's nodal conjecture (1982), for smooth metrics
achievement.context: Before: analytic metrics only (Donnelly–Fefferman, 1988); smooth surfaces had $\lambda^{3/4-\beta}$
achievement.note: Analytic metrics and the lower bound are untouched

voice.text: Still lines of a vibrating surface should grow like the square root of the frequency.
In higher dimensions, trapped vibrations glue into modes with huge zero sets.
Claimed: true on surfaces, false above.

sources.quote: Yau's problem section (1982). Donnelly-Fefferman (Invent. 1988): both bounds for real-analytic metrics
surfaces upper bound C lambda^{3/4} (Donnelly-Fefferman, Dong), improved to lambda^{3/4 - beta} by Logunov-Malinnikova
(i) on every smooth closed surface, H^1(zero set) <= C(M,g) sqrt(lambda)

(ii) fixed smooth metrics on S^3 (arbitrarily C-infinity close to round) and on S^2 x T^2 with eigenfunctions whose nodal measure / sqrt(lambda) -> infinity; (iii) a fixed smooth metric on S^4 x S^1 with nodal measure >> lambda^{1/2 + eps_0}
Counterexamples are for smooth (non-analytic) metrics only; Donnelly-Fefferman remains for analytic metrics. Lower bound untouched (Logunov).
All three directions are Comparator challenges with sorry-free solutions
I did not build the Lean library (no compilation allowed)
